description_full: Meritage Homes Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, designs and builds single-family attached and detached homes in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Homebuilding and Financial Services. It acquires and develops land; and constructs, markets, and sells homes for entry-level and first move-up buyers in Arizona, California, Colorado, Utah, Texas, Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. The company also provides title and escrow, mortgage, insurance, title insurance, and closing/settlement services to its homebuyers. Meritage Homes Corporation was founded in 1985 and is based in Scottsdale, Arizona.

financial_summary: Meritage Homes Corporation is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $4.4B market cap.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 22% against a 10% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $93M in free cash flow, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.26×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 9.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares.

The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 41%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $26.39 to $41.56 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 67% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 2.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 10.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $70.62 on average, 4% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 22% clears the cost of capital of 9.8% by 12pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.55).

hlth: The company holds more cash than debt.

It has missed earnings estimates by 6.5% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.6%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).

It returns 9.5% a year to shareholders (6.7% in buybacks and 2.8% in dividends).
